post.summary: Create a forge connection, writing its credential through to the secret store (ADR-0060)
post.description:
This is the manual/UI half of part D and the reason Forgejo can be onboarded
at all: GitHub registers itself when the App is installed, but a Forgejo
instance has no such event, so without this endpoint its only route into the
registry was a hand-written database row.

The credential is **write-only** in the strong sense — it is written before
the connection row exists, never read back by any endpoint, and the response
carries only the generated handle. Order matters: writing the secret first
means a failure leaves an orphan secret (harmless, overwritten on retry)
rather than a connection whose credential never landed (a live row that
silently cannot authenticate).

get.summary: Diff a connection's granted permissions and subscribed events against what Scarab needs (ADR-0060)
get.description:
This exists because both halves of a misconfigured GitHub App fail
*silently*:

 - **No events subscribed.** GitHub delivers `installation` /
   `installation_repositories` regardless, so the connection registers
   itself and `GET /v1/repos` looks healthy — while no push ever starts a
   run. The operator's only signal is that nothing happens.
 - **No `statuses:write`.** Every status post 403s while the run itself goes
   green, so the forge simply never shows a check.

Until now the only defence was documentation. `GET /v1/connections` already
answers "does the credential resolve"; this is the same question one level
deeper — *and is it allowed to do the things Scarab will ask of it*.

A live forge round-trip, so it is its **own endpoint** rather than fields on
the list: rendering Settings must not fan out a call per connection
unasked-for (the same reasoning that made `supports_resync` kind-derived
rather than probed).

It answers **200 with `status: "unknown"`**, not 501, when the adapter cannot
introspect. "Unknown" is a real health state the UI must render next to the
credential line, and the requirement list is still worth showing; a 501 would
force every caller to invent that state itself.

Never returns credential material — only names, levels and event ids.

post.summary: Bind a repo to a connection, creating its Project, and register its webhook (ADR-0060)
post.description:
There is no `projects` table: a Project *is* a `forge_repos` binding
(ADR-0046), so this endpoint is the repo→Project onboarding flow — "Enable"
on the org's repositories page — for every forge. After it, the repo appears on `GET /v1/repos`, can hold
Environments and secrets, and its pushes resolve to a tenant. A GitHub
installation makes its repos available but binds none of them, so this is
the GitHub path too.

Registration is attempted **after** the binding lands and its failure is
*reported, not rolled back*: the binding is the durable governance fact, a
hook is a remote side effect on a system that may be momentarily unreachable,
and unbinding on a failed hook call would delete a Project an admin just
asked for. `POST …/repos/{owner}/{name}/webhook` retries.

delete.summary: Unbind a repo from a connection, removing its Project (ADR-0060)
delete.description:
The inverse of the bind above, and destructive in the same measure: the
binding is the Project, so its Environments, scoped secrets and RBAC go with
it. That is why re-sync never does this on a forge's say-so and why this is an
explicit, human-addressed endpoint. It is permanent: no installation delivery
or re-sync binds the repo again; only another explicit bind does.

The forge-side webhook is deliberately **left in place**. Deleting hooks is
not in the port (ADR-0046 exposes registration only), and a stale hook is
harmless: an unbound repo's deliveries resolve to nothing and are dropped.

post.summary: Report the repos the forge reaches that are not enabled, and move this org's Projects off connections that do not serve it (ADR-0060)
post.description:
Enabling a repository is opt-in, so re-sync **creates no Project**. A repo
the forge reports that is not bound is listed in `available`; an admin
enables it from the org's repositories page (`POST
/v1/connections/{id}/repos`). A repo an admin disabled therefore stays
disabled.

The one change it makes is to an existing Project: a repo of this
connection's Org that is bound through a connection that does not serve
its owner (unassigned, or another Org's) moves to this one, with its
Project (git-bug 19b0a45). That is how an Org takes its repos back from a
legacy connection.

It **never unbinds**. Unbinding on a forge's say-so would let one failed
API page delete governance — Environments, secrets and RBAC hang off a
Project — so removal stays an explicit human act. `confirmed` reports the
overlap so a stale binding is still visible.

delete.summary: Delete an org Environment, with its overlays, grants and secrets when asked (ADR-0071)
delete.description:
Refused (409) while any Project holds an overlay or privilege grant in
it (ADR-0071 §3, §8: those are never dropped as a side effect), and while
any Project holds a secret in it (git-bug 52964b4): a secret never
outlives its Environment, and is never dropped as a side effect either.
The refusal's JSON body lists them, with a count per kind.

With `?cascade=true` the admin asks for them to go too (git-bug
a144fb1): every Project's overlay and privilege grant, deleted with the
Environment and its eligibility in one transaction, and the
Environment's secrets. The secret store cannot share that transaction,
so the secrets are deleted first, under the Environment's name claim
(no secret write into the Environment can land meanwhile). If a secret
delete or the transaction fails, the Environment stays, and a retry
deletes what is left. What was deleted, by name, is recorded on the
operation's `op.completed` event in the OrgSecurityEventLog.

post.summary: Duplicate an org Environment, its rules, eligibility, overlays, grants and secrets
post.description:
Not copied, and listed in the answer: Policies that select the old
Environment and not the new one, the Projects whose Pipelines name the
old one (from Run history), and the OIDC subject cloud trust policies
match. Run history, approvals included, and the Cache stay with the old
Environment, which is not changed.

The secret store is a separate store from the Environment's, so the two
cannot share a transaction. The secrets are copied first; the
Environment, its eligibility, overlays and grants are then created in
one transaction. If either step fails, the copied secrets are deleted, so
no partial Environment is left. A crash between the two leaves only
secrets under a name no Environment has, which no Run can resolve and
which a retry refuses (409) until an admin deletes them. The new name is
claimed throughout: a second Duplicate to it is refused (409) before it
writes anything, and so is a create of it by the Environment PUT, so no
other Environment takes the name while this one's secrets are written.

post.summary:
Approve a `manual` gate (ADR-0008, 0037). The authenticated principal's
approval is recorded on the event log (append-only, idempotent).
post.description:
An **Environment approval gate** (ADR-0078 §1: a Step after it uses the
Run's Environment's authority) releases only once the accumulated
approvals satisfy the Environment's effective rules for the run's Project
(ADR-0071 §3, `admits`) and its wait timer has run out on the gate's wait
clock (§4). Approvals that complete the rules early are kept: the gate is
released by the scheduler when the timer runs out. On release the
deployment is written to the legacy history. Every other `manual` gate is
a plain gate: it releases on the first approval, with no step-up. If the
Environment no longer exists or no longer admits the Project, no gate of
the Run releases (409). Authz'd as a write.

202.description: approval recorded: the gate released, or it waits for more approvals or for its wait timer

403.description: the caller may not approve (insufficient role), a step-up is required (`step_up_required`, JSON), or a `gate.resolve` Policy refused the approval or holds the gate (plain text naming the Policy)

404.description: no such run or gate

409.description: not an approvable gate (not a manual gate, not pending, or not reached yet), or the run's Environment no longer exists or no longer admits its project

429.description: an API token or Bearer session already has 10 step-up confirmation requests waiting (ADR-0073 §6)

post.summary: Reject a waiting gate: fail it with a reason (ADR-0070 §9).
post.description:
For any gate — `manual`, `timer` or `external` — that is pending and
reached (every step it needs has succeeded; slice b, criteria 2 and 3).
The gate's Attempt fails with
the reason and the rejecting principal, its dependents are skipped, and the
run ends `failed`; retrying the gate opens a new wait that asks again.

Authz'd as a run write, the same as approve. A reject only ever stops a
deploy — any writer can already cancel the run — so it does NOT consult the
Environment's approver rules, and it works when the Environment is gone or
no longer admits the project: the clean way out of a held gate.

202.description: this call rejected the gate: `{"rejected": true}`

400.description: missing, empty or over-long reason

404.description: no such run or step

409.description: not a rejectable gate, not pending, or not reached yet

post.summary:
Release an **external** gate by presenting its token (ADR-0034) — the path an
outside system (a deploy webhook, a change-management tool) uses instead of an
interactive approval. The token is `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{run}:{step}")`
(`sha256=<hex>`), verified in constant time; no per-gate storage. The endpoint
is 404 when no token secret is configured, and only releases gates of kind
`external` (manual gates stay approval-only). In a Deploy Run, the gate is
held (409) when the run's Environment no longer exists or no longer admits
its Project (ADR-0071 §2) — the same check `approve_gate` makes. The token
proves who is releasing, not that the deploy is still allowed.
post.description:
The same token can instead **fail** the gate with a reason: a body of
`{"passed": false, "reason": "…"}` rejects it (journalled `by
external:{step}`). A fail is never held — it only stops the deploy — so it
skips the Environment check. No body, or `"passed": true`, is a release.

requestBody.description: external gate (`x-scarab-gate-token`): optional, `{"passed": false, "reason": "…"}` fails the gate instead of releasing it. Plugin gate (a plugin's `scarab-api` bearer token, ADR-0076 §7): a `PluginGateRelease`, `{"attempt", "passed": true, "outputs": {…}}` or `{"attempt", "passed": false, "reason": "…"}`

202.description: gate released (or, with a fail body, failed)

400.description: malformed body, or a fail without a 1..1024-byte reason

404.description: no such external gate, or token release disabled

409.description: the gate is not pending or not reached yet, or (a release) the run's Environment no longer exists or no longer admits its project

The pin acts on the cold tier's **time** bound only. It says nothing about the

AboutDto.description:
The server's version and how this deployment runs, for the web UI's About
page. Names what is configured, never a secret or a URL with credentials.

commit.description:
The git commit the server was built from. `None` for a build that did
not record one (a local build).

executor.description: Where steps run: `k8s` (one Pod per step) or `local` (host processes).

github_app.description: The server runs a GitHub App (`SCARAB_GITHUB_APP_ID` is set).

login.description: People sign in through an OAuth/OIDC provider.

role.description:
Which part of Scarab this process runs: `converged` (all of it), `api`,
`scheduler` or `executor`.

started_at.description: When this server process started, in unix milliseconds.

ApiTokenDto.description: One issued token, as the API describes it — record only, never the secret.

created_by.description: Who minted it: a Principal's handle.

last_used_at.description:
Unix-ms of the last request that presented it, written back at most once
a minute. `None` means it has never been used.

owner.description: That Principal, as people read it.

owner_subject.description:
The id of the Principal who holds the token and whose live authority
bounds it (ADR-0080).

revoked_at.description: Unix-ms revocation, or `None` while it is live.

role.description:
The granted ceiling, not the effective role — what the token can do
depends on what its owner holds at the moment of each request.

use_count.description:
How many requests have presented it. Approximate: calls are counted in
memory and written in batches, so the count can lag by up to a minute,
and a server that stops loses the calls it had not written yet.

ApprovalGateRulesDto.description:
An Environment's settings for its Environment approval gate (ADR-0078
§3): the `manual` gate that has a Step using the Environment's
authority after it.

added_gate_expiry_s.description:
Seconds before the gate the Environment adds expires; absent = it
waits until approved or rejected.

max_approval_age_s.description:
Seconds an approval stays good for: a Step that uses the
Environment's authority is refused at launch once its approval gate
released longer ago than this. Default 86400 (24 hours).

required_approvals.description:
How many of the baseline's approvers must approve; absent = every
one. A Project overlay's approvers are each required as well.

ArtifactDto.description:
One artifact **version** in a run's list (ADR-0052, immutable per attempt
by ADR-0056). `step`/`attempt` are the publishing provenance (empty
strings on pre-ADR-0056 rows); `succeeded` is that attempt's verdict;
`of_record` marks the version the bare name-addressed download resolves
to — the latest successful version of that name.

org.description:
The Org the connection is to serve: the forge owner whose
repositories it binds.

AttemptDto.description:
One attempt at executing a step (ADR-0047) — the rerun unit. A step with more
than one attempt is one that failed-and-retried (or was restarted); the last
attempt carries the current outcome.

failed.description:
`true` if this attempt ended in a classified failure. A later attempt may
still have succeeded — that divergence is exactly the retry story worth
showing. Retained for back-compat; prefer `outcome` for the full picture
(a `superseded`/`cancelled` attempt is `failed:false` but NOT green).

failure.description:
Coarse failure kind when `failed`: `infra` | `step` | `timeout` | `lost`
| `config` | `missing-inputs` (an input snapshot gone from every tier —
Rerun/Retry regenerates it; ticket e140121) | `gate` (a gate's wait
resolved failed — e.g. not released within `gate_expires_after`; the
reason is in `failure_detail`).

failure_detail.description:
The executor's human-readable cause for a failed attempt (ticket
4cf03d7) — e.g. "cold tier refused: connection refused" — alongside the
machine-consumed `failure` class. Absent = the class is the whole story
(or a pre-0041 row). Stored since migration 0041.

outcome.description:
The attempt's recorded outcome (ADR-0056 amendment): `running` |
`succeeded` | `failed` | `superseded` | `cancelled`. Unlike `failed` this
distinguishes a *superseded* attempt (a rerun/retry replaced its input
while it was still running and its Pod was torn down) from a genuine
success — so the UI never renders an abandoned attempt green.

AuthProviderDto.description: One login provider, as the login page offers it (ADR-0069).

default.description: The one used when a login names none.

AvailableRepoDto.description:
`GET /v1/connections/{id}/available-repos`: what the connection's credential
reaches, and which of those Scarab already governs.

bound.description:
Already a Project on this connection — the bind form renders it as done
rather than offering a no-op that silently re-homes a live binding.

BindRepoRequest.description: `POST /v1/connections/{id}/repos` body: the repo to bring under governance.

register_webhook.description:
Also create the forge-side webhook, so a push actually reaches Scarab.
Defaults to **true**: a bound repo with no hook is a Project that silently
never builds, which is not a state anyone asks for on purpose.

BindRepoResultDto.description:
The outcome of binding a repo: the Project it created, and what happened to
the webhook.

org.description:
The governed Project's natural key — `(owner, name)` in v1 (1 Project : 1
RepoRef), the same mapping every bind uses.

webhook_error.description:
Why it did not, when it did not. The binding still stands — see the
handler's note on why a hook failure is reported rather than rolled back.

webhook_registered.description: Did a forge-side webhook get registered (or already exist)?

claimed.description:
`false` = created by a forge import and not signed into yet — the
Members panel's "not signed in yet". Absent when the store does not
know the subject.

display_name.description:
The Principal's display name, when the identity store knows it
(ADR-0069).

handle.description: The Principal's handle (`github:alice`): what people read and type.

id.description: The Principal's id (ADR-0080): what a member's URL carries.

origin.description:
Who wrote the binding: `native` (granted in Scarab, which a forge
re-sync never changes) or `import` (seeded from the forge's
collaborators, which a re-sync refreshes or removes). Set on the org
listing; absent on an import's response, which lists what the forge
gave and not what each row holds.

BoundInputDto.description: One input in the scope of a Step's invocation.

bound.description: The literal value, or the template text.

kind.description:
`literal` (a value known at compile: the caller's literal or the
input's default) or `template` (the caller's `${{ … }}`, rendered at
launch).

BrokerJournalEntryDto.description:
One row of an installation's broker journal: a request its plugin sent to
the CredentialBroker, and what the broker did with it.

bytes.description: Response body bytes delivered to the plugin (`end` rows).

denied_reason.description: Why the broker refused it, or why its stream ended short (`cut: …`).

duration_ms.description: Until the refusal, the response head, or the end of the body.

id.description: The row's id; pass the last one of a page as `before` for the next.

path.description: The request path after the slot, as the plugin sent it.

query_keys.description:
The names of the query parameters, in order. Their values are not
returned: on a refused row the query is stored as the plugin sent it.

request_id.description: Ties a request's `head` row to its `end` row.

rule.description: The read rule that admitted it (`GET /api/v1/applications/*`).

slot.description: The connection slot the request named (it may name no real slot).

started_at.description: When the request reached the broker (Unix ms).

status.description: The status the plugin got: the upstream's, or the broker's refusal.

upstream_path.description:
The path forwarded upstream; absent when it was refused before a read
rule matched.

BrokerJournalPage.description: A page of an installation's broker journal, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to read the next, older page; absent on the last.

BrokerJournalPhaseDto.description:
One phase of a broker journal row. `refused`: the broker answered the
request itself and sent nothing upstream. `head`: it forwarded the request
and the upstream's response head arrived. `end`: that response's body
ended. A forwarded request has a `head` and an `end` row with the same
`request_id`.

CapabilityRequirementDto.description:
One capability Scarab needs of a forge app, as the preflight reports it
(`scarab_forge::preflight::ForgeRequirement` on the wire).

level.description:
Minimum level for a permission (`read`/`write`/`admin`); absent for an
event, which is subscribed or not.

name.description:
The forge's own name for it (`statuses`, `push`) — the label on the
setting an operator has to go and change.

CatalogEntry.description:
One pipeline in the dispatch catalog: its selection `name` and whether it
opts into `manual` / `api` dispatch (its `on:` includes that trigger).

api.description: This pipeline declares `on: api` — its programmatic dispatch sibling.

error.description:
Set when this single file failed to parse — the rest of the catalog still
lists (a broken sibling does not fail the whole listing, ADR-0043 §4).

manual.description: This pipeline declares `on: manual` — it appears in the human catalog.

name.description:
The bare selection name (e.g. `deploy`) — what a describe/dispatch call
passes as `pipeline`.

CompileErrorDto.description:
One compile error with the fields a reader acts on (ADR-0076): the Step,
the command index and the template it reads, and for a library Step the
library and the caller's binding. `message` is the compiler's text.

bound.description: For a library Step: the caller's `with:` value for `input`.

input.description: For a library Step: the library input the caller binds.

kind.description:
`command_value` (a `command` argument reads free text from outside
the Pipeline), `script_template` (a `${{ … }}` in a script) or
`other`.

library.description: For a library Step: the library (its installed name or a path).

library_step.description: For a library Step: its id inside the library.

step.description: The Step in the Pipeline file; for a library Step, the invoke Step.

CompileErrorResponse.description:
`400` body for a Pipeline that does not compile: the whole text, as a
plain-text 400 carried it before, and each error with its fields.

sha.description: The commit the Pipeline was read at.

credential.description:
The browser's `AuthenticationResponseJSON`, from a passkey of the
Principal being merged in.

ConnectionDto.description:
One registered forge connection, as global Settings renders it (ADR-0060).

Carries the credential's **handle and whether it resolves** — never the
material. A connection is the unit an operator reasons about ("is my GitHub
App still wired up?"), so the DTO answers that without becoming a way to read
a secret back.

account_id.description:
The forge's immutable id of the account the connection serves (a
GitHub installation's `account.id`), recorded from its installation
delivery; `null` until one arrives, and for every other kind.

account_login.description:
That account's login, for display: refreshed on every installation
delivery, so a renamed account shows its current name. Never what
decides which Org the connection may serve (`account_id` does).
`null` until a delivery records it, and for every other kind.

base_url.description: The API base URL the adapter talks to (GHES / a self-hosted Forgejo).

credential_present.description:
Does `credential_ref` actually resolve to material right now? The single
most common breakage (a DB restored without its secrets, a reseed that
never happened) is invisible until a run fails — this surfaces it.

credential_ref.description:
The `_forge`-scoped handle the credential lives under. An opaque name,
not the secret.

enabled_repos.description:
How many repositories are enabled through this connection: its repo
bindings, each a Project (ADR-0046). A count, not the list: a
connection can hold thousands. The org's repositories page
(`GET /v1/orgs/{org}/repos?connection=`) lists them.

installation_id.description:
The GitHub App installation this connection is (`github-install-<n>`);
`null` for every other kind.

last_delivery_at.description:
Unix-ms of the most recent accepted webhook delivery from this **forge
kind**, if any. Deliveries are recorded per kind (the ADR-0046 replay
guard is keyed that way), so with two connections of one kind this is a
per-kind liveness signal, not a per-connection one.

managed_by_config.description:
Is this connection managed declaratively (config-owned) and therefore
read-only here (ADR-0060 part D)? A connection has exactly one owner —
the `connections:` config or the database — and this says which, so the
UI never offers an edit the next boot would silently revert.

org.description:
The Org this connection serves (git-bug 19b0a45); `null` = unassigned,
visible to and editable by global admins only.

supports_preflight.description:
Can this connection's app configuration be checked against what Scarab
needs (`GET …/preflight`)? Decided from the kind, like `supports_resync`
and for the same reason: the check is a live forge round-trip, so the
list must not perform one per row just to discover the button is
pointless. The endpoint itself remains the authority.

supports_resync.description:
Can the forge enumerate what this credential reaches? Gates the re-sync
affordance: GitHub can, so a drifted registry is healable; an adapter that
cannot should not offer a button that always errors.

web_url.description: The forge's own web host, for deep links out of the UI.

ConnectionPreflightDto.description:
The result of checking a connection's app configuration against what Scarab
needs (ADR-0060 preflight) — the deeper cut of the same question
`credential_present` answers on the list.

Carries **no credential material**: granted permissions are names and levels,
events are names. Nothing here can authenticate to anything.

checked.description: Did the forge actually answer? `false` for every `unknown`.

granted_permissions.description:
What the forge says the app *is* granted, including grants Scarab does
not need — an operator comparing against the App settings page wants the
whole picture, and an over-broad grant is worth seeing.

missing.description:
The subset of `required` the forge does not currently grant. Empty on
`ok`, and (necessarily) empty on `unknown` — read `status`, not this.

required.description:
Everything Scarab needs from this forge, so the answer is legible even
when nothing could be checked.

status.description:
`ok` — every required capability is granted; `degraded` — at least one is
missing (runs will silently not trigger, or checks will silently not
post); `unknown` — the forge could not be asked. Three values, not two:
"I could not look" must never render as "you are fine".

subscribed_events.description: The webhook events the forge will deliver, as it reports them.

unavailable_reason.description:
Why the check could not run, when it could not — an adapter that cannot
introspect, a credential that does not resolve, a forge that errored.

ConnectionSlotDto.description: A named external system the plugin reaches through the broker.

ConsumedDto.description:
What an attempt consumed (ADR-0056): the map `upstream step id → attempt
id` stamped at its launch — the durable answer to "which generation of
`build` did `test` actually build on?" after a mid-run restart leaves the
run a patchwork of attempt generations. `attempt` names the attempt the
map belongs to; empty map = nothing recorded (no upstream evidence, or a
pre-ADR-0056 attempt).

CreateConnectionRequest.description:
`POST /v1/connections` body (ADR-0060 part D, manual path): the forge to
connect and the credential to reach it with.

`credential` is **write-only** — it is written through to `SecretProvider`
under a server-generated handle and never appears in any response. There is
deliberately no "update the credential" field on the read DTO: a secret you
can read back is a secret you have leaked.

base_url.description:
The instance root Scarab talks to (e.g. `https://codeberg.org`). A
trailing slash is normalized away.

credential.description: The forge access token. Write-only (see the struct docs).

kind.description:
`forgejo`. GitHub is not creatable here — installing the App *is* its
registration (ADR-0060 part C), so a create form for it could not work.

org.description:
The Org the connection serves (git-bug 19b0a45): the forge owner whose
repositories it binds. The caller must administer it; the first
connection of an Org that does not exist yet needs a global admin.

policy.description:
The authored Policy (ADR-0075 §4). At the Project level it must be a
typed `setting` (§7).

reason.description: Why, recorded on the PolicyVersion. At most 2,000 bytes.

CreateRunRequest.description:
`POST /v1/runs` body: an inline pipeline to run immediately, plus any launch
parameters (ADR-0043) declared by the pipeline's `interface`.

params.description:
Supplied launch parameters, `name → value` (ADR-0043). Resolved against
`pipeline.interface.inputs` at creation: coerced to the declared types,
defaults applied, validated fail-closed. Absent = none supplied.

reason.description:
Optional caller-supplied **reason** for this inline run (ADR-0057 §3),
stamped as the run **Headline** (`trigger_title`) for this `api`-style
dispatch. Accepted and stamped verbatim, no requiredness check. Absent =
no headline.

CreatedConnectionDto.description:
`POST /v1/connections` response: the created connection's id and the
generated handle its credential now lives under. Not the credential.

credential_ref.description:
The server-generated `_forge`-scoped handle. Echoed so an operator can
correlate the row with its secret; it is a name, not a value.

DispatchKind.description:
Which trigger a dispatch opts into: a human [`Manual`](DispatchKind::Manual)
dispatch (the default) or its programmatic [`Api`](DispatchKind::Api) sibling
(ADR-0043 §4). The named pipeline must declare the matching `on:` trigger to
be dispatchable.

DispatchRequest.description:
`POST /v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/dispatch` body: dispatch a **named** pipeline at
a `ref`, supplying its declared launch parameters (ADR-0043 "World B"). Unlike
the inline `POST /v1/runs` escape hatch, this rides the read-at-ref → compile
→ admission machinery — a dispatched deploy hits Environment governance.

kind.description:
Which trigger to dispatch: `manual` (default) or `api`. The pipeline must
declare the matching `on:`.

params.description:
Supplied launch parameters, `name → value` (ADR-0043). Resolved against
the pipeline's `interface.inputs` at the resolved commit: coerced,
defaulted, validated fail-closed. Absent = none supplied.

pipeline.description:
The pipeline to run — a `.scarab` name (e.g. `deploy`) or a full
`.scarab/*.yaml` path.

reason.description:
Optional operator-supplied **reason** for this dispatch (ADR-0057 §3),
stamped as the run **Headline** (`trigger_title`). The endpoint accepts and
stamps it verbatim — it performs **no** requiredness check; requiredness is
an Environment `ProtectionRule` enforced at admission (thread D). Absent =
no headline.

ref.description:
The ref to dispatch at (branch/tag/sha). Resolved to a concrete commit;
the run pins to that commit.

privilege_grants.description: Projects whose privilege grant was copied.

secrets.description: The EnvironmentProjectSecretScope secrets copied, with their values.

DuplicateNotCopiedDto.description: What a duplicate left for an admin to do by hand.

new_oidc_subject.description:
The same for the new Environment: a cloud trust policy matching
`old_oidc_subject` must also match this one before a Run here can
assume its role.

notes.description: Other things the copy does not carry, one sentence each.

old_oidc_subject.description:
The OIDC subject a Run in the old Environment presents
(`*` for the repository and the ref).

policies.description: Policies that apply to the old Environment and not to the new one.

projects_with_runs.description:
Projects whose Runs named the old Environment (from Run history):
their Pipeline YAML names it, and runs in the new one only once it is
changed.

DuplicateOrgEnvironmentRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{org}/environments/{env}/duplicate`: the new
Environment's name and, optionally, its display name.

display_name.description:
Omitted, empty or blank: what the old Environment shows, plus
" (copy)".

name.description:
The new Environment's name: the key its pipelines will name. The
name rule of a created Environment applies.

DuplicateOrgEnvironmentResponse.description:
The answer to a duplicate: the new Environment, what was copied and the
checklist of what was not.

DuplicatePolicyDto.description:
A Policy a duplicate did not change: its `match.environments` selects
the old Environment and none of its patterns selects the new one.

project.description: The Project it is attached to; `null` for an org Policy.

DuplicatedSecretsDto.description: One Project's secrets the duplicate copied, by key. Never a value.

EffectiveProtectionDto.description:
The rules admission enforces for one Project in one Environment: the
baseline merged with the Project's overlay (ADR-0071 §3), computed by the
server so no client re-implements the merge.

allowed_ref_layers.description:
One list per layer (baseline first, then overlay): a ref must match
**every** non-empty layer. Never pre-intersected — `[main]` and
`[tags/*]` intersect to `[]`, which would read as "any ref".

approvers.description: Baseline approvers, then the overlay's not already listed — all required.

wait_timer_s.description:
The longer of the two layers' wait timers. It does nothing when
`approvers` is empty.

EnvironmentDeleteBlockersDto.description:
Why a plain delete was refused (409): what the Environment still holds.
`?cascade=true` deletes all of it with the Environment.

overlays.description: Projects holding an overlay in it.

privilege_grants.description: Projects holding a privilege grant in it.

EnvironmentEligibilityDto.description:
Which Projects may run Deploy Runs into an Environment (ADR-0071 §2):
every Project in the org, or exactly those matching one of `projects`
(project-name globs, `*` wildcards).

all_projects.description: Every Project in the org. `projects` must then be empty.

projects.description:
Project-name globs, matched ignoring ASCII case. Stored trimmed; a
pattern of only `*` is refused (use `all_projects`), and so is one
listed twice. An empty list with `all_projects: false` admits **no**
Project — eligibility starts closed.

EnvironmentProjectDto.description: One Project's standing in one Environment, for the Environment's admin.

eligible.description: Whether the Environment's eligibility admits it now.

EnvironmentProjectPrivilegeGrantDto.description: The privileges one Project holds within one Environment (ADR-0071 §8).

EnvironmentProjectSecretKeysDto.description: One Project's secrets in an Environment, by key. Never a value.

EnvironmentProtectionRulesDto.description:
Protection rules as one layer holds them — an Environment's baseline or a
Project's overlay (ADR-0071 §1, §3).

allowed_refs.description: Ref globs a deploy's symbolic ref must match; empty = any ref.

oneOf.description:
The Environment approval gate's settings (ADR-0078 §3). Present on a
baseline only: an overlay has none.

approvers.description:
Principal handles (stored as ids, ADR-0080). Every one must approve
(AND), unless the baseline's `approval_gate.required_approvals` says
how many of its own must.

require_reason.description: A human dispatch must carry a reason (ADR-0057 §3).

wait_timer_s.description:
Seconds: a minimum wait on the Environment approval gate, counted on
the gate's wait clock (ADR-0078 §4). It does nothing where the
effective approvers are empty; a client shows that from `approvers`
(here, or `effective.approvers` for a Project).

ExpiredInputDto.description: One expired Workspace Snapshot behind a widened rerun (ADR-0061 s5).

consumer.description: The step whose input workspace is incomplete.

produced_by.description: The upstream step that produced the missing snapshot.

root.description: The CAS merkle root the store no longer holds.

ExternalGateVerdict.description:
Optional `POST /v1/runs/{id}/gates/{step}/release` body: an external gate's
verdict. Absent (or `passed: true`) releases the gate; `passed: false`
fails it with `reason`.

passed.description: `false` fails the gate; `true` (the default) releases it.

reason.description:
Why the gate failed — required (1 to 1024 bytes, trimmed) with
`passed: false`; ignored on a release.

connection.description:
A ForgeConnection id, for a private repository. Omitted: fetched
anonymously over https.

name.description:
The library name, as `invoke: lib:<name>` will write it: parts of
letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, joined by `::` or `/`, each part
starting with a letter, digit or `_`. Defaults to
`<owner>::<repo>::<file name without its extension>`.

ref.description:
A branch, tag or commit, for a `source` with no `@<commit>`. Scarab
reads the file at the commit it points to now; the stored version and
the answer's `source` name that commit.

connection.description:
A ForgeConnection id, for a private repository of the org. Omitted:
read anonymously over https from github.com or a Forgejo
connection's host.

source.description:
The plugin's manifest file, `<host>/<owner>/<repo>//<path>@<commit>`;
the path ends in `.json`, `.yaml` or `.yml`.

FetchPluginUpgradeRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{org}/plugins/{name}/upgrade-fetch`: which manifest to
read for the upgrade. Either `source`, or `commit` to read the file the
installation's recorded source names at that commit.

commit.description:
A full commit id (40 or 64 lowercase hex). Read when `source` is
omitted; the installation must have a recorded source then. There is
no branch resolution: the admin names the commit.

connection.description:
A ForgeConnection id to read it through. Omitted with `source`: read
anonymously. Omitted with `commit`: the connection the recorded source
was read through.

image.description:
The image the upgrade would run, `<repository>@sha256:<64 hex>`. When
given, it is checked against the new manifest's named repository, and
`needs_step_up` is judged with it: any image other than the installed
one needs a step-up. Omitted: judged as keeping the installed image.

source.description:
The new manifest's source, `<host>/<owner>/<repo>//<path>@<commit>`.
Omitted: the recorded source's file at `commit`.

oneOf.description:
What is installed under this name now, if anything: pass its hash as
`replaces` to upgrade.

diff.description:
The change from `current`, one line per entry, each starting with
`+`, `-` or a space. Empty when nothing is installed.

FetchedPluginManifestDto.description: A plugin manifest read for review. Nothing is stored or installed.

installed.description:
The org's installations of the same plugin (`manifest.plugin`), by
name, each with the manifest hash it was approved with.

manifest.description:
What the plugin asks for: what an install approves with the image
digest.

source.description: The source as read, pinned to its commit.

FetchedPluginUpgradeDto.description: A manifest read for an upgrade, and what it changes. Nothing is stored.

connection.description: The connection it was read through: pass it to `…/upgrade`.

current_manifest_sha256.description:
The installed manifest's hash: pass it to `…/upgrade` as
`expected_current_sha256`.

needs_step_up.description:
Whether `…/upgrade` asks for a step-up: exactly when there is a
reason. Decided again by the server at the upgrade.

source.description: The source as read, pinned to its commit: pass it to `…/upgrade`.

step_up_reasons.description:
Why `…/upgrade` asks for a step-up, each as a sentence: what the new
manifest asks for that the installed one did not, and a new image
(any digest other than the installed one is new code). Judged with
the request's `image`, or the installed image when it has none.
Empty = a narrowing on the same image, which needs none.

GateApprovalDto.description: The answer to a gate approval.

approvals.description:
The approvers recorded on the gate so far. Absent when the gate had
already released.

released.description: The gate has released (now or before this approval).

releases_at.description:
When the gate releases (epoch ms): the approvals are in and the
Environment's wait timer is still running. Absent otherwise.

GateDefinitionDto.description:
A gate a plugin resolves: a Pipeline waits on it with `invoke:
plugin:<installation>/<name>`.

outputs.description: What the plugin returns when it releases the gate.

GateFieldDto.description: One input or output of a gate definition, with its type.

required.description: Whether a Pipeline must pass it (always true for an output).

GateOutputDto.description: One output a plugin gate returns on release.

value.description: The value the plugin released the gate with; absent until then.

GateResolutionDto.description: How a gate's wait resolved: its `GateResolved` journal entry.

attempt.description: The gate Attempt the verdict closed (`a1`, `a2`, …).

by.description:
Who rejected it, for a rejection by request (`external:{step}` for an
external gate's token). Absent for a verdict the engine reached.

passed.description: `true`: the gate passed and its dependents may run.

reason.description: Why — a timer elapsing, an expiry, a rejection's reason.

GithubAppDto.description:
How this server takes GitHub connections: whether it runs a GitHub App,
and the page that App is installed from.

app_mode.description:
The server runs in GitHub App mode (`SCARAB_GITHUB_APP_ID` is set), so
installing the App on an account registers that account's connection.
`false`: GitHub connections cannot be added from the web UI.

install_url.description:
Where an admin installs the App (`https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new`).
`None` when not in App mode, or when GitHub could not be asked.

unavailable_reason.description:
Why `install_url` is missing in App mode: the App key does not resolve,
or GitHub answered with an error.

GrantedPermissionDto.description: A permission the forge reports as granted.

IdentityMergeDto.description: A merge waiting for a passkey of the Principal it folds in.

from.description: The Principal that would be folded into the caller.

passkeys.description: How many usable passkeys `from` holds; one of them must answer.

provider.description: The sign-in that proved it: its provider and handle.

merged.description:
The Principal folded into the caller; `null` when the sign-in was
attached without a merge (its Principal let go of it since the link
started) or already was the caller's.

removed_passkeys.description: How many of its passkeys the merge deleted.

ImageGrantDto.description: One entry of a privilege whitelist (ADR-0039).

capabilities.description: The Linux capabilities it may add.

image_digest.description:
`sha256:…` — the digest a step's image must be pinned to
(`repo@sha256:…`). Matched exactly.

privileged.description: May run as a privileged container.

content_hash.description: A version fetched into this org.

name.description: The library name to install under, as `invoke: lib:<name>` writes it.

replaces.description: The hash installed now (an upgrade), or omitted for a first install.

config.description: Values for the manifest's `config_keys`; omitted = none.

connection.description: The connection the fetch read it through, if any.

manifest_sha256.description:
The `manifest_sha256` the fetch returned, which the admin reviewed.
The install is refused (409) when the source no longer reads as it.

name.description:
The installation's name: a DNS-1123 label, unique in the org and
never reused once uninstalled.

source.description:
The manifest's source, as `POST …/plugin-fetch` read it. Read again
here.

oneOf.description: A PersistentVolumeClaim to mount (ADR-0074 §7); omitted = none.

InstallationStateDto.description: Whether an installation's broker calls are accepted.

InstalledPluginManifestDto.description: An installation of the plugin a fetch read.

id.description:
10 lowercase hex, minted at the first install and kept by upgrades.
What the settings page's URL carries.

name.description: The library name, as `invoke: lib:<name>` writes it.

oneOf.description: The installed version is yanked in this org.

cancelled_runs.description: The Runs a yank with `cancel_runs` cancelled. Omitted otherwise.

name.description: The library name the yanked version was fetched for.

source.description: The git source the version was fetched from, pinned to its commit.

provider.description: The login provider to link an account from (`GET /v1/auth/providers`).

LinkIdentityResponse.description: Where the browser goes to prove the account.

csrf.description:
The session's CSRF token — browsers echo it in `x-csrf-token` on every
mutation (also delivered as the readable `scarab_csrf` cookie).

handle.description: The Principal's handle: what people read.

ManifestDiffDto.description: The installed manifest against the new one, group by group.

gates.description:
Gate names; a gate whose definition changed is both removed and
added.

image.description: The image repository the manifest names.

read_rules.description:
`<slot>: <method> <path>[ ?<query keys>]`. One more allowed query key
is a new rule.

ManifestDiffGroupDto.description: One group of an upgrade's manifest diff.

MeResponse.description: The authenticated principal (ADR-0049) — powers the UI's identity menu.

admin_orgs.description:
The orgs this principal may administer, for the Settings area to act on.
One entry in practice (single implicit Org, ADR-0060) — a list because
`Org` remains the model's real inheritance root, not a collapsed
constant. Empty on a fresh install: an org only exists once a Project is
bound to it, so `can_administer` can be true with nothing to administer
yet.

can_administer.description:
May this principal administer org-level settings (ADR-0060)? The gate on
the global Settings area — the UI hides the nav entry when false, since
nothing there is actionable or informative without `Administer`.

True for a globally-`Administer` role, or an `Admin`+ binding on the Org
scope of any org the caller can see. Deliberately *not* implied by a
Project-scoped `Administer`: administering one repo does not grant the
org's secrets or its forge connections (ADR-0049 — Org inherits down,
never up).

display_name.description: Human display name, when the identity provides one.

global_admin.description:
Does the caller hold a global `Administer` role? Only such a caller
may add the first connection of an Org that does not exist yet, or
act on an unassigned connection (git-bug 19b0a45). Always `false` for
an API token.

handle.description: The Principal's handle (`github:alice`): what people read and type.

id.description: The same id, under the name every person response uses.

identities.description:
The provider accounts this Principal can sign in with (ADR-0069).
Empty when no identity store is wired (dev).

subject.description: The Principal's id (ADR-0080): stable, random, never shown as a name.

token_mint_orgs.description:
The orgs this principal may mint a personal API token in, sorted: every
org where they hold a role binding (org or project), and every org for
a bootstrap owner. The mint still checks the role in the exact scope.
Always empty for an API token, which may not mint.

can_enroll_first.description:
No usable passkey yet, and this browser session's login is fresh
enough to enroll the first one.

fresh_login_until.description: Until when this session's login is fresh (a browser login only).

fresh_login_url.description:
Where this human logs in again — through the login provider they sign
in with — landing on enrollment (a relative URL). The one place the
provider is chosen: `scarab security setup` prints this.

handle.description: The caller's handle: what to sign in as.

has_passkey.description: Holds at least one usable (not clone-flagged) passkey.

passkeys.description: The passkeys — empty for an API-token caller (see `passkeys_hidden`).

passkeys_hidden.description:
The caller is an API token: a token, scoped to one Org or Project,
never reads its owner's passkey list (only whether one is held).

usable_passkey_count.description: How many usable (not clone-flagged) passkeys are held.

window_expires_at.description: This browser session's open window, if any (unix ms).

MemberDto.description:
`GET /v1/orgs/{org}/members/{id}`: one person and the roles they hold in
the org (ADR-0080 §5). The member page reads this by the Principal's id.

bindings.description: Their bindings in the org, org scope first, then by repository.

claimed.description:
`false` = created by a forge import, not signed into yet. Absent
when no identity store knows them.

MintOwnTokenRequest.description:
`POST /v1/me/tokens` body: [`MintTokenRequest`] plus the org, which the
personal route cannot take from its path.

name.description: Human label — what makes the token revocable in practice.

org.description: The org the token is scoped to (or the org of its project).

project.description: Project within the org to scope the token to. Absent = the whole org.

role.description:
The **ceiling**: `viewer` | `member` | `admin` | `owner`, never more
than the caller holds in this scope.

MintTokenRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{org}/tokens` body. Every field is required on purpose: a
credential with no verb and no expiry is the shape this repo already learned
not to mint twice.

expires_in_days.description: Lifetime in days, `1..=365`. No default and no "never".

name.description:
Human label — what makes the token revocable in practice. "demo
keepalive", "amy's laptop".

project.description:
Project within the org to scope the token to. Absent = the whole org,
inheriting down to its projects exactly as an org binding does.

role.description:
The **ceiling**: `viewer` | `member` | `admin` | `owner`. Never more than
the minter holds in this scope, and capped again at each request by what
the owner holds *then*.

MintedTokenDto.description: The mint response — the **only** place the plaintext ever appears.

record.description: The token's record, for immediate display in the list it just joined.

token.description:
The credential. Returned once, here. Scarab keeps only its SHA-256, so
this exact string cannot be recovered from the database, from a backup,
or by any later API call: a lost token is re-minted, never re-read.

MissingGateModeDto.description:
What Run creation does when a Step that uses the Environment's authority
has no `manual` gate upstream (ADR-0078 §3).

OpSummary.description:
What a human is asked to confirm: the server-rendered, redacted
description of one operation (shown in the 403, on the confirm page and
in the event log).

changes.description: What changes, one line each. Redacted fields read `(hidden)`.

operation.description: What is being done ("Write a secret").

OrgEnvironmentDto.description: An org-level Environment in its minimal shape (ADR-0071, MMP step 1).

display_name.description: What people see in place of the name; `null` shows the name.

eligibility.description:
Which Projects may deploy here. Read-only here: written through
`…/eligibility`.

name.description: The key pipeline YAML and the OIDC subject use. Fixed once created.

protection.description:
The baseline every Project's Deploy Runs obey. Read-only here:
written through `…/protection`, never by the whole-Environment PUT.

updated_by.description: Who last wrote it (a Principal's handle).

trusted_sources.description:
The library sources this org trusts, one entry per source and grant
(ADR-0076 §9, ADR-0018 amendment of 2026-11-12). No library is
trusted without one.

OrgRepoDto.description:
One repository of an org: enabled (a Project, bound through a connection)
or reachable through one of the org's connections and not enabled.

can_change.description:
May the caller enable or disable it here? Needs Administer on the
connection's org, and a connection not managed by configuration.

connection_id.description:
The connection it is bound through when enabled, else the one that
reaches it: the `{id}` of the bind and unbind endpoints.

enabled.description: Is it a Project? Enabling binds it; disabling unbinds it.

project.description: The Project's name when enabled (the repo name).

repo_url.description: The repository's page on the forge.

unreachable_since.description:
For an enabled repo: unix-ms since when its connection has not
reached it (the GitHub App's installation stopped covering it), or
`null`. Disable is the only way to remove it.

OrgReposPageDto.description: `GET /v1/orgs/{org}/repos` response: one page of the org's repositories.

can_administer.description: Does the caller administer the org?

enabled_total.description: How many of the org's repositories are enabled, whatever the query.

total.description: How many repositories match the query, across every page.

unlisted.description:
Connections whose repositories could not be listed. Their enabled
repositories are still in the list; the ones not enabled are not.

admins_without_passkey.description:
Admins of the Org (Admin/Owner bindings on the Org, and — for a
global administrator only — the bootstrap owners) who hold no usable
passkey: every crown jewel is refused for them until they enroll one.

enforced.description: Step-up is enforced on this install.

pending_requests.description: StepUpConfirmationRequests waiting for a human in this Org.

recent_refusals.description: The last 20 refusals in the Org, from the last 24 hours.

unresolved_owner_entries.description:
Bootstrap owners entries that match only a verified email at login
and name no Principal: not counted above, since no passkey is ever
stored under one (a global administrator's view; 0 otherwise).

OriginLinkDto.description: One link of a Step's invoke chain, outermost first.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the library source (or of the plugin's approved manifest).

kind.description:
`file`, `library`, `plugin`, or `environment` for the gate an
Environment added to the Run (ADR-0078 §2).

name.description:
A repo-relative path (`file`), the library name (`library`) or the
plugin installation and gate (`plugin`).

source.description: Where an installed library comes from, at its commit.

yanked.description: The version is yanked in the Run's org now.

OrphanedSecretsDto.description:
Secrets one Project holds under an Environment name that has no
Environment. Names only, never values.

backup_eligible.description: The credential may be synced to other devices (BE).

backup_state.description: It is backed up / synced, as last seen (BS).

clone_suspected.description: Its signature counter went backwards: it is never accepted again.

label.description: A name for the passkey ("MacBook Touch ID"). Default `Passkey`.

subject.description: The id of the Principal whose passkeys were reset.

windows_revoked.description:
How many standing step-up confirmations (windows, unconsumed action
confirmations) were revoked.

PendingGateDto.description: One open wait of a plugin gate.

attempt.description:
The wait's Attempt: a release names it, and an answer to another wait
is dropped.

expires_at.description: When the wait expires and fails (Unix ms).

gate.description: The gate's name in the plugin's manifest.

inputs.description: The gate's inputs, rendered when it was reached.

step.description: The gate's step id in the Run.

next.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last.

PersonDto.description: A person as an API response names them (ADR-0080 §5).

id.description:
The Principal's id: what a URL carries. For a reference that names
no Principal, the reference itself.

PipelineCatalogResponse.description:
`GET /v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/pipelines?ref=` body: the manually-dispatchable
catalog at a ref (ADR-0043 §4). Lightweight — each entry is an `on:`-only
read, not a full compile. `sha` is the ref resolved to a concrete commit.

pipelines.description:
Every `.scarab/*.{yaml,yml}` at the commit (excluding `.scarab/lib/**`
and files marked `kind: library`), path-sorted.

sha.description:
The ref resolved to a concrete commit — the catalog reflects this exact
commit, and a subsequent describe/dispatch should pin to it.

budget.description:
Opt-in run budget in seconds (ADR-0047): the run fails once its
**active** time (gate-suspended time excluded) exceeds this. No default.

interface.description:
The pipeline's launch/reuse interface (ADR-0038, 0043) — its declared
typed parameters (`inputs`) and exposed outputs. Carried as the pure
`scarab_pipeline::Interface` (opaque object in the schema; the pure crate
cannot derive `ToSchema`). Absent = no parameters.

PipelineInterfaceResponse.description:
`GET /v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/pipelines/{name}/interface?ref=` body: the
compiled, typed launch-parameter schema for ONE selected pipeline (ADR-0043
§4). A pure function of the compiled IR — the same compile path dispatch
rides — so the form and the run validate against byte-identical specs.

api.description: This pipeline opts into `api` dispatch (`on: api`).

inputs.description:
The declared typed launch parameters (name, type, required, default,
options, validate, description) — the compiled `interface.inputs`.

manual.description: This pipeline opts into `manual` dispatch (`on: manual`).

sha.description:
The ref resolved to a concrete commit — the interface reflects this exact
commit; a subsequent dispatch should pin to it.

PlanReasonDto.description: Why a step is in a rerun plan (git-bug 4afaa3e).

PlannedStepDto.description: One member of a rerun plan, with its WHY (git-bug 4afaa3e).

because_of.description:
The in-set step this one is here because of: the cascade parent
(minimum in-set need by id, deterministic) or, for `regenerate`, the
consumer whose expired input dragged it in. Absent only on the target.

is_gate.description:
A gate (ADR-0008): the rerun pauses for approval here — the plan never
claims a gate will run.

reason.description: Why it is in the set.

step.description: The step that re-runs (a gate re-arms and pauses instead of running).

PluginCapabilityDto.description: One entry of the closed PluginCapability vocabulary (ADR-0072 §2).

PluginConnectionDto.description:
One connection slot of an installation and what an admin bound to it
(ADR-0072 §5). Never carries the credential, nor its secret key.

auth_schemes.description: The schemes the manifest allows; `bearer` is the only one today.

base_url.description: Where every request on it goes — and nowhere else.

ca_pem.description:
The CA certificates (PEM) that are the ONLY trust anchors for
`base_url`; absent = the platform's roots. Certificates are public.

configured.description:
Whether an admin has bound it. Unbound, the broker answers the
plugin's requests on it with 409.

credential_set.description:
Whether the credential is present in the secret store. Write-only:
no endpoint returns it.

insecure_http.description:
`base_url` is plain `http://`: the credential crosses the network in
the clear. Allowed (an in-cluster Service, say); the UI warns.

read_rules.description: What the plugin may send through it: reads only.

attempt.description: The wait being answered, as the pending-gates query listed it.

outputs.description: A release's outputs: exactly what the gate declares, each of its type.

passed.description:
`true` releases the gate with `outputs`; `false` fails it with
`reason`.

reason.description: Why the gate failed: 1 to 1024 bytes, required with `passed: false`.

PluginGateViewDto.description: What a `gate: plugin` node waits on, and where its wait stands.

expires_at.description: When the latest wait expires (Unix ms).

gate.description: The gate's name in the plugin's manifest.

inputs.description: The inputs rendered when the gate was reached; absent before.

plugin_state.description: `enabled` or `killed`; absent when the installation is gone.

releaser.description: The Principal that may release it: `plugin:<installation>`.

waiting_since.description: When the latest wait began (Unix ms).

id.description: Server-minted, 10 hex; names the installation's ServiceAccount.

name.description: Unique in the org and never reused.

plugin.description: The plugin's own name, from its manifest.

principal.description: `plugin:<name>` — what it acts as in audit.

probe_passed_at.description: Unix-ms the isolation probe last passed.

source.description:
Where the approved manifest was read,
`<host>/<owner>/<repo>//<path>@<commit>`. Absent for an installation
made before the source was recorded.

source_connection.description:
The ForgeConnection the source was read through; absent = read
anonymously, or not recorded.

oneOf.description: The PersistentVolumeClaim its Pod mounts (ADR-0074 §7); absent = none.

PluginManifestDto.description:
What the plugin asks for — exactly what an admin approves with the
digest (ADR-0072 §1-2).

gates.description:
The gates the plugin resolves (ADR-0076 §7), by name; empty without
`resolve_gates`.

image.description:
The image repository the plugin ships as, when the manifest names
one: an install or upgrade must run an image of it. Absent = the
manifest does not name its image, so any repository is accepted.

PluginStorageDto.description:
An installation's storage (ADR-0074 §7): a PersistentVolumeClaim an
operator created in the plugin namespace. Scarab mounts it read-write; it
never creates, backs up or reads it.

claim.description: The claim's name in the plugin namespace.

mount_path.description: Where the Plugin's container sees it.

owner_annotation.description: The annotation the claim must carry before the runtime mounts it…

owner_annotation_value.description:
…and its value, `<org>/<installation name>`. The plugin namespace is
shared by every org; this is how the operator says which
installation the claim is for.

claim.description:
The PersistentVolumeClaim's name in the plugin namespace (a DNS-1123
subdomain). Scarab does not create it.

mount_path.description:
An absolute path in the Plugin's container; omitted = `/data`. Not
`/`, and clear of `/tmp`, `/var/run/secrets` and the other paths the
runtime or the kubelet mounts.

policy.description: The draft Policy, as `POST …/policies` takes it.

yaml.description:
The draft as YAML, such as a `kind: policy` file pasted into the
editor. At most 64 KiB.

PolicyCheckResponse.description: What checking a draft found. Nothing is saved.

diagnostics.description: Errors first, then the `has()` warnings of the rules that compiled.

ok.description: No error: saving this Policy at the org level would compile it.

policy.description:
The draft as `POST …/policies` takes it: what `yaml` parsed to (with
`kind` dropped), or `policy` itself. Absent when the body is not a
Policy.

rules.description: Each rule that compiled, with the input fields it reads.

PolicyCheckpointDto.description: One PolicyCheckpoint as the policy editor needs it.

effects.description:
The effects a Policy saved here may use. Only `deny` is evaluated
today, at every checkpoint.

match_keys.description:
The `match` keys a Policy here may set: `projects`,
`except_projects`, `environments`, and `trigger_kinds` at
`run.create` only.

schema.description:
The input schema: `variables` (the CEL variables a rule reads), and
`structs` and `enums` by name. Each field has `name`, `ty` (`{kind,
of}`), `optional`, `max_len` and `doc`.

trigger_kinds.description: The values `match.trigger_kinds` takes; empty where it is refused.

denied.description: It denied, or a rule failed while it was enforced (which denies).

would_deny.description: In audit mode it would have denied, or a rule failed.

policies.description:
One per Policy whose `match` selected at least one decision since
then, by id.

PolicyDecisionPageDto.description: One page of the org decision log, newest first.

next.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; absent on the last one.

decision.description:
The PolicyDecision: `checkpoint`, `schema_version`, `input`,
`policy_set_digest`, `results` (one per Policy: `policy_id`,
`version`, `name`, `level`, `mode`, `outcome`), and `outcome`
(`{kind: allow}` or `{kind: deny, messages}`).

run_id.description: The Run the decision admitted; absent for a refused `run.create`.

at.description:
Where in the Policy: `name`, `match.projects`, `rules[0].when`,
`rules[0].message`. Empty when the body is not a Policy.

expr.description: The sub-expression the finding is about, as the checker renders it.

line.description:
1-based line and column in the rule's `when`; 0 for a finding that
is not about CEL.

PolicyDto.description: A stored Policy, at its current version.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 of the Policy's canonical JSON.

deleted.description: Deleted Policies keep their history and are not consulted.

project.description: The Project of a Project typed setting; absent at the org level.

version.description:
1 on create; each save, the delete included, adds one. A PUT or
DELETE names it as `expected_version`.

rules.description: Empty when the stored Policy no longer compiles.

limit.description:
How many of the newest decisions at the draft's checkpoint to read
(default and cap 200).

policy.description: The draft Policy, compiled at the org level.

policy_id.description:
The stored org Policy the draft edits: each decision's `before` is
that Policy's part in it. Absent for a new Policy: `before` is
`allow`.

PolicyReplayResponse.description:
What a draft would change over the recorded decisions. Nothing is
enforced or recorded.

changed.description:
The decisions whose outcome for this Policy would change, newest
first.

evaluated.description: Decisions the draft was evaluated against.

read.description: Decisions read: the newest at the checkpoint, at most `limit`.

skipped.description:
Decisions not evaluated: no recorded input (the Run was over an
input list cap), or an input of a schema version this server does
not evaluate.

PolicyTestPipeline.description:
The Pipeline form of the policy test: what `scarab validate --server`
sends.

libs.description:
Every `file:` library the Pipeline invokes, transitively: repository
path (`.scarab/lib/deploy.yaml`) to source.

path.description:
The Pipeline file's repository path; the Pipeline's name when it
declares none. Default `.scarab/ci.yaml`.

project.description: The Project the Run would be created in.

PolicyTestRequest.description:
`POST /v1/orgs/{org}/policy-test`. Name at most one of `policy` and
`policy_id` (neither: the Project's effective Policies), and exactly one
of `input`, `decision_id` and `pipeline`.

checkpoint.description:
The checkpoint of `input`: `run.create`, `step.admit` or
`gate.resolve`. Default: the checkpoint of `policy` or `policy_id`,
else `run.create`. A recorded decision is at its own checkpoint, and
a `pipeline` builds a `run.create` input.

decision_id.description: A recorded decision of this org, whose input is evaluated again.

input.description: A checkpoint input, as a PolicyDecision records it.

oneOf.description: A Pipeline to compile here and build the input from.

policy.description:
A draft Policy, compiled at the org level. Needs Administer on the
org; stored Policies need Read on the input's Project (an org Policy
by id, Read on the org).

policy_id.description: A stored Policy of this org (either level).

decision.description:
The PolicyDecision, as admission would record it (see
[`PolicyDecisionRecordDto::decision`]). A draft Policy has
`policy_id` "" and `version` 0.

policies.description: Per evaluated Policy, what each rule reads.

actor.description:
The forge account that caused the event. Default: the caller for
`manual` and `api` (as a dispatch is), none otherwise.

actor_id.description:
The forge's immutable id of that account (a webhook's `sender.id`),
which admission resolves to the linked Principal (ADR-0069); webhook
kinds only. Default none: the Run has no `principal`.

fork.description: A pull request from a fork; `pull_request` only. Default false.

reason.description: The dispatch reason; `manual` and `api` only. Default none.

ref.description:
The symbolic ref, as admission sees it: `refs/heads/main` for a push,
a dispatch or a cron fire (the default branch), `refs/pull/<n>/head`
for a pull request, `refs/tags/<tag>` for a tag or release. Required
for those kinds; `comment` has none, and for `upstream` it is the
upstream Run's ref, if any.

PolicyVersionDto.description: One saved version of a Policy (ADR-0075 §11).

author.description: The handle of the Principal who saved it.

step_up_ref.description: The StepUpConfirmation that approved this save, when one was needed.

PrincipalDto.description: A Principal, as the grant/approver typeahead offers it (ADR-0069 §3).

claimed.description: `false` = created by a forge import, not signed into yet.

handle.description: What a grant or an approver entry is typed as.

id.description:
The Principal's id (ADR-0080): what a grant or an approver entry
stores, and what a URL carries.

handle.description: The person's handle there today (login / email) — display only.

ProjectDto.description: One registered project (governed repo, ADR-0046) in the repos list.

connection_id.description:
The forge connection it is bound through: the `{id}` of
`/v1/connections/{id}/…`, and the row of `GET /v1/connections` that
says whether it is managed by configuration.

last_run_at.description:
Epoch millis of the project's most recent run, or `null` if it has never
run — the dashboard's recency signal (ADR-0046). The domain carries no
push/created_at yet, so never-run repos have no ordering key here.

owner.description: The forge coordinate backing it (1:1 in v1).

repo_url.description:
The forge WEB base for this repo (e.g. `https://github.com/owner/name`) —
what the UI appends `/commit/<sha>` or `/pull/<n>` to for deep links.
Derived from the connection's kind + base_url (the stored base is the API
host, which differs from the web host on GitHub).

unreachable_since.description:
Unix-ms since when its forge connection has not reached it (the
GitHub App's installation stopped covering it), or `null`. The
Project is kept; its events are ignored and no run can start until
the forge covers it again or an admin disables it.

ProjectEnvironmentDto.description:
An org-level Environment as one Project sees it (ADR-0071): the read
model behind `GET /v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/environments`, which until
ADR-0071 returned the repo's own per-repo environments.

baseline.description: The Environment's baseline, set by an org admin.

display_name.description: What people see in place of the name; `null` shows the name.

effective.description: What admission enforces: the baseline merged with the overlay.

eligible.description:
Whether this Project may deploy here now (EnvironmentProjectEligibility).
`false` only for an Environment the Project still holds an overlay or
grant in after an admin made it ineligible.

oneOf.description: This Project's tighten-only overlay, if it has one.
This Project's privileges here, if an admin granted any.

PutApprovalGateRules.description:
The approval gate settings of a baseline `PUT` (ADR-0078). Each omitted
field takes its default.

added_gate_expiry_s.description:
Seconds before the gate the Environment adds expires; omitted = it
waits until approved or rejected.

max_approval_age_s.description: Seconds an approval stays good for at launch; omitted = 86400.

required_approvals.description:
How many of `approvers` must approve, 1 to their number; omitted =
every one.

PutEnvironmentProjectOverlayRequest.description:
A Project overlay (`…/projects/{project}/overlay`) body: the baseline's
four rules, which can only **tighten** (ADR-0071 §3). Replaced whole,
omitted = permissive default, unknown fields refused — as for the
baseline.

PutEnvironmentProjectPrivilegeGrantReque.description:
A Project's privilege grant (`…/projects/{project}/privilege-grant`)
body, replaced whole.

permit_k8s_overlay.description: May the Project's steps here set a raw `k8s_overlay` (ADR-0055).

privileged_images.description: The ADR-0039 whitelist; each digest listed once.

PutEnvironmentProtectionRequest.description:
A baseline (`…/protection`) body: the four rules and the approval gate
settings, replaced whole. Every field is optional and an omitted one
takes its default — never the stored value — so `{}` resets the baseline
to permissive (and the approval gate settings to theirs).
Unknown fields are refused, so the retired per-repo shape (`wait_timer`,
`concurrency`) — and `deployment_concurrency`, which ADR-0074 removed — is
a 400, not a silently ignored rule.

approval_gate.description:
The approval gate settings, in the shape `GET` returns them under
`protection.approval_gate`. Omitted = every default.

approvers.description:
Principal handles or ids (ADR-0069, ADR-0080): each must name an
existing Principal; a merged one is stored as the Principal it now is.
All must approve.

require_reason.description: A human dispatch must carry a reason (ADR-0057 §3). Omitted = off.

wait_timer_s.description:
Seconds: a minimum wait on the Environment approval gate (ADR-0078
§4). Refused (400) above 0 with no approvers.

PutOrgEnvironmentRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/environments/{env}`: the whole Environment, replaced.
An omitted optional field takes its default — it does not keep the stored
value. Unknown fields are refused, so a misspelt field — or one ADR-0074
removed (`deployment_deadline_ms`, `deployment_sources`) — is a 4xx rather
than silently ignored.

display_name.description:
What people see in place of the name. Omitted, empty or blank shows
the name. Changing it never needs a step-up: the name, which pipelines
and cloud trust policies refer to, stays.

PutPluginConnectionRequest.description:
`PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/plugins/{name}/connections/{slot}`: bind the slot's
destination and credential, replacing any previous binding whole.

base_url.description:
`https://host[:port][/prefix]` (or `http://`, warned about). Every
request the plugin sends on this slot goes here; it cannot pick
another host.

ca_pem.description:
PEM CA certificates to trust INSTEAD of the platform roots, for an
internal CA (https only). There is no skip-verify.

credential.description:
The bearer token the broker adds upstream. Required on every bind —
a new destination never inherits a credential entered for another —
and never readable back.

PutSecretRequest.description:
`POST /v1/secrets` body: define (or overwrite) a secret at a scope. The
`value` is **write-only** — no endpoint ever returns it.

repo.description: Repo, for a repo- or environment-scoped secret.

value.description: Secret value — stored envelope-encrypted, never returned.

RefDto.description:
One branch or tag: its kind, bare name, and the short SHA of the commit it
points at (a resolved-SHA hint for the picker row). The full SHA is
intentionally omitted — selecting a ref re-resolves it through the pipelines
endpoint, which is the authority on the pinned commit.

name.description: The bare ref name (no `refs/{heads,tags}/` prefix), e.g. `main`, `v0.3.1`.

short_sha.description: The 7-char short SHA of the commit the ref points at.

RefsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/repos/{org}/{repo}/refs?q=` body: the repo's branches and tags for a
searchable ref picker (ADR-0046). Scoped to branches + tags — recent commits
and open-PR head-refs are a deliberate follow-up, not part of v1.

refs.description: Branches first, then tags; each group name-sorted.

RefusedRunDto.description: A trigger that did not become a Run.

errors.description: Each error: for `compile` with its fields, otherwise its message.

reason_kind.description:
`compile`, `yanked`, `policy`, `environment`, `event_field`,
`forge_token`, `schedule` or `upstream` (a loop or too long a chain
of follow-ups).

title.description: The trigger's headline: a push's commit subject, a dispatch reason.

RejectGateRequest.description: `POST /v1/runs/{id}/gates/{step}/reject` body: why the gate is failed.

reason.description:
The human reason, journalled on the gate's verdict and its Attempt.
Required: 1 to 1024 bytes once trimmed.

RenderedSpecDto.description: A Step's image, command and env as its launch renders them.

before.description:
`allow`, `deny` or `would_deny`: the stored Policy's part in the
recorded decision, or `allow` when it had none.

messages.description:
The messages of the draft's rules that matched, or why one failed;
empty when `after` is `allow`.

run_id.description: The Run the decision is about; absent for a refused `run.create`.

step_id.description: The Step and attempt of a `step.admit` decision.

RequestRuleDto.description:
An allowed read on a connection: method + path pattern (`*` = one
segment) + the query keys it may carry.

query.description:
The query keys a request under this rule may carry, each at most
once; empty = no query. Anything else is refused by the broker.

RerunPlanResponse.description:
`GET …/steps/{step}/rerun-plan` body: what a rerun/retry of this step would
actually execute — **before** the user confirms it (ADR-0061 s5, and
ADR-0027's rule that smart never means mysterious).

A read-only dry run. The interesting case is a widened one: a Run reopened
after its Workspace Snapshots expired cannot rerun just the step you pointed
at, because the inputs that step consumes no longer exist — so the scope
expands upstream to regenerate them, in the limit back to `clone`. That is a
bigger action than the button implies, so it has to be visible first.

expired_inputs.description:
Each expired input that caused the widening: the consuming step, the step
that produced the missing snapshot, and its CAS root.

invalidated.description:
Every step that would re-execute, sorted — the invalidation set after any
widening.

starts_from.description:
The steps the rerun effectively **starts from** (no dependency inside the
set). `[target]` on an ordinary rerun; on a widened one this is the phrase
the affordance says out loud — "this re-runs from *clone*".

steps.description:
The same set as `invalidated`, **execution-ordered** and carrying each
member's WHY (git-bug 4afaa3e) — computed by the engine, identically for
this preview and for the plan a POST rerun/retry executes and returns.

target.description: The step the plan is for.

widened.description:
The subset of `invalidated` present only because a Workspace Snapshot
expired: upstream steps dragged in to regenerate data. Empty on an
ordinary rerun.

ResyncResultDto.description:
`POST /v1/connections/{id}/resync` body: what the forge reports, compared
with what is enabled.

available.description:
Repos of the connection's Org the forge reports that are not enabled.
Re-sync does not enable them; an admin does, from the org's
repositories page.

confirmed.description:
How many bindings the forge confirms. Reported rather than acted on:
see the handler's note on why re-sync never unbinds.

moved.description:
Repos that were already Projects, bound through a connection that does
not serve their owner (unassigned, or another Org's), and now bound
through this one with their Projects (git-bug 19b0a45).

skipped.description:
Repos the forge reports that are neither available nor moved: owned by
another account than the connection's Org, already bound through
another connection that serves an Org, or reported to a connection that
serves no Org yet.

index.description: The rule's index in `rules`; 0 for a typed setting.

reads.description:
The input fields a CEL rule reads (`trigger.ref`, `steps`); empty for
a typed setting, which reads Step and gate origins.

display_name.description:
What headings show in its place; absent when it has none or the org
no longer has an Environment of that name.

RunListResponse.description: `GET /v1/runs` body: the most recent runs, newest first.

oneOf.description:
The Environment the Run names (its pipeline's `environment:`), with
its display name. Absent for a Run that names none.

origin_pr_base.description:
The PR **base** branch (ADR-0057) — the branch a `pull_request` run
targets, rendered `base ← head` in the ref cluster. A discrete origin
